item.title: 🚨WARNING: GOG & MAGOG Will Explode at Any Moment | Rabbi Tovia Singer
item.description:
Something extraordinary is unfolding in the Middle East right now, and Rabbi Tovia Singer explains why he believes the war between Iran and Israel is directly connected to the prophecy of Gog uMagog in Ezekiel 38–39. Why does Ezekiel identify Persia as a central player in the final conflict? Why does Sukkot appear at the heart of the biblical vision of redemption? And are we watching a process described by the prophets thousands of years ago unfold before our eyes?
Follow the official Parsha Inspired WhatsApp Channel for new videos and live updates: https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VbDuN4T9xVJeoI6ySU09
In this conversation, Rabbi Tovia Singer explores Gog uMagog, Iran, Sukkot, the clouds of glory, Daniel 7, Mashiach and the stages of the final redemption — and explains why he believes the events surrounding Israel today fit into a much larger biblical process.
We discuss:
• Why Rabbi Singer identifies the current Persia–Israel conflict with Ezekiel 38–39 • Why Ezekiel describes Persia among the nations involved in the final war • Why Rabbi Singer says redemption unfolds in stages rather than happening all at once • Why the events since October 7 have caused so many Jews to return to Torah and teshuvah • The meaning of the “hooks” in Ezekiel 38 and why Rabbi Singer connects them to Iran • Why he believes Iran continues to push deeper into a conflict it could otherwise avoid • The extraordinary connection between Gog uMagog and Sukkot • Why “Gog” is connected to the idea of a roof — and what that means spiritually • Why the sukkah represents trusting in Hashem rather than material protection • The clouds of glory that protected the Jewish people after the Exodus • Why Zechariah 14 says the surviving nations will one day celebrate Sukkot in Jerusalem • How Daniel 7 connects the kingdoms of history, the clouds of heaven and Mashiach • Why Rabbi Singer says Ezekiel reads as though the prophet were watching events happening in our own time • The extraordinary danger Israel faced from Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas and the Houthis • Why Rabbi Singer says Israel was facing an existential threat • The connection between October 7, Sukkot and the larger process of redemption • Why the prophets describe the nations ultimately recognizing the God of Israel • What all of this may mean as we approach another Sukkot
Rabbi Singer explains that Gog uMagog is not simply one sudden event disconnected from everything that came before it. The prophets describe a process in which Israel returns to its land, enemies gather against it, the Jewish people awaken spiritually, the nations witness the hand of God, and ultimately Mashiach and the final redemption emerge.
According to Rabbi Singer, the events unfolding around Israel today deserve our attention because Ezekiel, Zechariah and Daniel describe a sequence that bears striking similarities to what we are witnessing now.
May we merit to see the protection of the Jewish people, the complete redemption, the coming of Mashiach and the rebuilding of the Beis Hamikdash speedily in our days.
Subscribe to @RabbiAronSokol for more Torah, Jewish prophecy, Mashiach, the Third Temple, Israel and the unfolding redemption.

item.title: The Shofar Is the Original Spiritual Alarm Clock
item.description:
In this clip, Rabbi Lawrence Hajioff explains why the shofar is far more than just a symbol of Rosh Hashanah.
The shofar is a mitzvah built around listening. Its raw sound represents the cry of the Jewish soul, a call to wake up, reflect, and recognize where we are heading. Rabbi Hajioff also explains the Rambam’s famous idea that the shofar is a spiritual wake-up call and how even one small action can tip the scales of a person’s entire year.
Sometimes the most powerful message has no words at all.

item.title: 🚨ALERT: Something BIG Is Happening Around Israel… And It’s Not Accidental

Since the war began, Israel has been pushed into the center of the world’s attention. We also discuss Rosh Hashanah, our relationship with God, the unique mission of the Jewish people, and why the events unfolding now may be pointing toward something far bigger than most people realize.

item.title: SHOCKING: The Case For The Oral Torah (Historical Proof)
item.description:
Why does Judaism have thousands of pages of Talmud and rabbinic law if the Torah itself says not to add or subtract from it? Rabbi Mordechai Becher joins Aron Sokol to explain what Judaism actually means by “Torah” — and why the Written Torah was never meant to stand alone.
Rabbi Becher is a longtime Torah educator whose classes are available on Torah Anytime and YU Torah, and he co-hosts the podcast *Two Rabbis on a Podcast*.
He explains:
Why Judaism believes there is both a Written Torah and an Oral Torah Why the biblical text cannot always be understood without a living tradition What ancient tefillin and mezuzot reveal about Jewish practice Why disagreements between rabbis do not mean the tradition was invented How rabbinic laws can prohibit something the Torah itself permits Why this does NOT violate the commandment not to add to the Torah How far Jewish law can actually change with changing circumstances Why the Sanhedrin was essential to applying Torah in every generation What separates legitimate disagreement from simply rewriting Judaism Why Judaism has remained recognizable across countries and thousands of years
00:00 Intro 00:11 Are There Really Two Torahs? 00:40 What Jews Actually Mean by “Torah” 03:06 Why the Written Text Alone Isn’t Enough 05:39 The Written Torah vs. the Oral Torah 08:00 Ancient Evidence for Jewish Tradition 10:27 Where Does the Torah Hint at an Oral Law? 12:16 Why Some Things Cannot Be Learned From a Book 14:10 Why the Oral Torah Was Kept Oral 16:29 How the Oral Torah Created the Jewish Culture of Learning 18:38 Why Rabbis Disagree 20:45 Why the Tablets Are Often Drawn Round 23:09 How Flexible Can Judaism Be? 25:44 Did the Rabbis Add to the Torah? 26:56 Tradition, Rabbinic Law and the Limits of Change 29:33 How Can There Be Different Opinions in Jewish Law? 31:46 The Rules That Limit Rabbinic Debate 34:03 What Are Judaism’s Red Lines? 35:42 What “Do Not Add to the Torah” Really Means 37:25 Why Rabbis Can Ban Something the Torah Permits 39:54 How Jewish Acceptance Creates Binding Practice 42:16 What Actually Counts as Judaism? 43:00 Why Jews Study Thousands of Pages of Talmud 43:51 A Blessing for the Jewish People
@TwoRabbisPodcast @InspiredIsrael ​

item.title: The Torah Says Jews Are Priests to the Nations
item.description:
Steve Eisenhower explains one of the most overlooked ideas in the Torah: if the Jewish people are called a “kingdom of priests,” then who are they priests to?
In this clip, Steve argues that Israel’s role is ultimately directed toward the nations of the world. He connects this idea to the biblical vision of the nations turning toward the Jewish people to learn about God, and to Israel’s mission as a light to the nations.
If Israel is the priesthood, then the nations are the congregation.
@Exodus_Project
#Torah #Judaism #Israel #Noahide #Bible #Prophecy

item.title: The Greek Word That Changed Isaiah 7:14
item.description:
In this clip, Steve Eisenhower breaks down one of the most important translation debates in the Bible: Isaiah 7:14 and the meaning of the Hebrew word almah and the Greek word parthenos.
Was the original prophecy really speaking about a virgin birth, or did the meaning of the Greek word change over time? Steve explains the historical and linguistic background, how parthenos was used in earlier Greek literature, and why this verse became so central to Christian interpretation.
One word can completely change how a prophecy is understood.
@Exodus_Project #Isaiah714 #Bible #Judaism #Christianity #Torah #Prophecy #Hebrew

item.title: 🚨WARNING: What’s Coming Next Is Worse Than You Think
item.description:
What if we are not waiting for Gog and Magog anymore?
Rabbi Efraim Palvanov argues that the prophetic sequence described in Ezekiel may already be unfolding before our eyes. Israel has returned. The land has revived. The Jewish people are gathering from exile. And the confrontation surrounding Iran and Persia may place us somewhere in Ezekiel 38 and 39 right now.
If that is true, the question is no longer whether prophecy is beginning.
The question is: what comes next?
In this powerful conversation, we walk through Ezekiel 36, 37, 38 and 39 and examine where we may actually stand in the redemption process.
Why does Persia appear in the prophecy of Gog and Magog? Could the events surrounding Iran be part of that process? What comes after Ezekiel 38 and 39? And why does Rabbi Palvanov say that we are now “very much at the finish line”?
We also explore one of the most extraordinary ideas in the entire conversation: could the resurrection of the dead eventually involve DNA, biotechnology or future forms of cloning?
In this episode:
• Why Rabbi Palvanov believes we are living in the pre-Messianic era • Ezekiel 36, 37, 38 and 39 • Why Gog and Magog may already be unfolding • The prophetic role of Persia and Iran • The return of the Jewish people to the Land of Israel • What happens after Ezekiel 38 and 39 • The Third Temple and the next stages of redemption • Could resurrection involve DNA and biotechnology? • Why Torah is spreading increasingly to the nations • Why the redemption process may be accelerating
If the prophetic timeline is really where Rabbi Palvanov believes it is, then what comes next could change everything.

Rabbi Yehuda Glick reveals the real preparations already taking place connected to the Beit Hamikdash — including Temple vessels that have already been prepared, Kohanim studying the laws of the Temple service, work on the priestly garments, and groups developing blueprints and practical plans for rebuilding.

In this conversation we discuss:
• The preparations already underway for the Third Temple • Temple vessels that have already been prepared • Blueprints and practical plans for rebuilding • Kohanim preparing for the Temple service • The dramatic changes taking place on the Temple Mount • Why Rabbi Glick believes more Jews must return to the mountain • The Temple Mount as a house of prayer for all nations • Jerusalem, redemption and biblical prophecy • What Rabbi Glick believes needs to happen next
For generations, rebuilding the Beit Hamikdash seemed impossibly distant.
Rabbi Glick believes that is changing.
His message is simple:
“It’s in our hands.”

item.title: God’s Redemption Plan Never Required Perfect People
item.description:

In this clip, Steve Eisenhower and I look at some of the most important figures in the biblical story of redemption, including King David, Bathsheba, Judah and Tamar, and ask why God repeatedly brings redemption through people whose stories include serious mistakes.
The Jewish answer is not that a person needs someone else to save them. A person can recognize what they did wrong, repent, and turn directly to Hashem.
Mistakes are not the end of the story. What matters is what you do next.

item.description:
The first day of Rosh Hashanah 2026 falls on Shabbat, and Rabbi Lawrence Hajioff explains why this year carries such a powerful message.
What is the real meaning of Rosh Hashanah? Why does the Torah describe it as a day of sounding the shofar rather than simply a “Day of Judgment”? And what does the shofar reveal about teshuvah, judgment, redemption and the year ahead?
In this conversation, Rabbi Lawrence Hajioff explores the deeper meaning of Rosh Hashanah, the spiritual significance of listening, and the teaching that Rosh Hashanah is a microcosm of the entire coming year.
We discuss:
• Why the shofar is the central Torah mitzvah of Rosh Hashanah • Why the shofar represents the inner cry of the Jewish soul • The shofar of Mount Sinai and the future shofar of redemption • The Rambam’s famous description of the shofar as a spiritual wake-up call • Why one mitzvah can change a person and impact the entire world • The remarkable lesson of Ishmael and “ba’asher hu sham” • Why a person is judged according to who they are right now • How teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah can change a difficult decree • The special significance of the first day of Rosh Hashanah 2026 falling on Shabbat • A blessing for a sweet new year, redemption and the rebuilding of the Third Temple
Rosh Hashanah is not simply about fear. It is about renewal. It is the moment when we stop, listen, examine who we are and recognize that the coming year can still be changed.
May we all be written and sealed for a Shana Tova U’Metuka, a good and sweet year filled with blessing, peace and redemption.

item.title: 🚨The REAL Reason Jews Still Reject Jesus
item.description:
Why have Jews rejected Jesus as the Messiah for almost two thousand years?
The answer is not that Jews have never heard about Jesus, refuse to read the Bible, or hate Christians. The real answer is that Judaism and Christianity disagree about what the Messiah is, what he must accomplish, whether a human being can be divine, and whether the Torah can ever be replaced.
In this episode, Rabbi Aron Sokol presents the Jewish position directly from the Hebrew Bible and the writings of Maimonides. The discussion follows the central framework developed by Rabbi Aryeh Kaplan in his classic work, The Real Messiah.
The prophets gave the Messiah a clear mission. He must gather the Jewish exiles, restore the kingdom of David, rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem, strengthen Torah observance, bring humanity to the knowledge of God, and establish real peace throughout the world.
The central question is simple: Did Jesus complete that mission?
This video examines:
• The traditional Jewish definition of Mashiach • Why Judaism teaches that the Messiah will be a human king • Maimonides’ test for identifying the true Messiah • Why Judaism does not accept the Christian doctrine of a second coming • How Christianity transformed the Messiah from a human leader into a divine redeemer • The Jewish response to original sin and salvation through belief • Why Judaism teaches personal responsibility, repentance and direct return to God • The Jewish interpretation of Isaiah 53 • Whether Jeremiah’s “new covenant” replaces the Torah • Why God’s covenant with Israel remains eternal • The influence of Paul on the development of Christianity • Why Jews for Jesus and Messianic Judaism are considered forms of Christianity • How Jewish survival became one of Judaism’s strongest historical answers • Maimonides’ remarkable teaching about the possible role of Christianity and Islam in preparing humanity for the final redemption
This is not an attack on Christians. Millions of Christians sincerely love God, the Bible and the people of Israel. This presentation explains why Judaism cannot accept the Christian claims about Jesus while still respecting Christians as human beings created in the image of God.
The main biblical passages discussed include Isaiah 2, Isaiah 11, Isaiah 52–53, Jeremiah 31, Ezekiel 18, Ezekiel 36–37, Zephaniah 3, Zechariah 14, Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 30. The criteria established by Maimonides can be found in Mishneh Torah, Hilchot Melachim, chapters 11 and 12.
If you disagree, share the verses you believe answer these questions:
Where does the Hebrew Bible say that the Messiah will divide his mission between a first and second coming?
Where does it say that God will become a human being?
Where does it say that the eternal Torah will be canceled or replaced?
Let’s discuss the texts honestly and respectfully.
Subscribe to Parsha Inspired for more conversations about Judaism, biblical prophecy, Israel and the unfolding redemption.
#judaism #jesus #messiah
